pages.title: Infinitesimal
pages.text: Smaller than every positive real, and yet not zero. Leibniz used them freely; Weierstrass banished them; Robinson brought them back rigorously as non-standard analysis. The grain looks like nothing at all, and the closer you look the further away it seems to be.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted the step size in a derivative to be truly smaller than anything. The Analytic Continuator pressed the real continuum against a quantum dot under superfluid helium, and squeezed out a number below every real but still above zero.
